gen-fs-styro-fs-supreme: Retro and commanding, Styro crams its lowercase letters together until the gaps nearly vanish. But Supreme holds its heavy shapes wide open, and that pinched-versus-open tension is the pair's draw.
gen-gf-bpmf-iansui-fs-bespoke-sans: Relaxed and hand-drawn, Bpmf Iansui moves in one steady line with no thick-thin shifts at all. And Bespoke Sans does the crisper job, keeping generous space between curve ends and the stem.
gen-gf-cause-fs-literata: Literata brings a bookish serif look, with sturdy thin lines and only slightly heavier thick ones. But Cause is the looser hand, with an e opened wide and diagonals matching its stems.
gen-gf-coming-soon-archivo: Coming Soon writes loose handwritten letters, with a ring-like o and lowercase rising close to the capitals. Archivo adds a commanding x-height, and that casual-versus-sturdy mix is the draw.
gen-gf-coming-soon-fs-asap: Readable and open, this sans keeps its c forms as arcs and its lowercase near capital height. Asap carries the text while Coming Soon adds casual, hollow glass-tube lettering on top.
gen-gf-coming-soon-fs-epilogue: Scribbled and friendly, Coming Soon leads with casual, hand-drawn letters. It does personality best, while Epilogue handles the quiet reading with a wire-like monoline skeleton and tall-bodied, curvy letters.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-fs-epilogue: Loose and friendly, Delius Unicase spaces its letters like rope-ladder rungs. Epilogue gives it a wire-like monoline partner with curvy, tall-bodied letters, and that loose-meets-tidy mix is the draw.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-fs-public-sans: Relaxed to the core, Delius Unicase keeps its line width through every turn. Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase and broad counters, so paragraphs of text move along comfortably.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-switzer: Hand-drawn warmth first: Delius Unicase never tapers a stroke end. Switzer does the tidy part best, with tubular, wire-like letterforms whose c tips never creep toward touching.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-work-sans: Blunt, friendly strokes define Delius Unicase, with a pronounced x-height and no tapering at the ends. And Work Sans, with its mean line set high, gives that warmth a modern, tidy counterpart.
